title: Congruence & Similarity
description: Identify congruent and similar shapes; use scale factors for lengths and areas.

notes.heading: Congruent Shapes

illustration.alt: Diagram showing two congruent triangles with matching side lengths and two similar triangles with different sizes but equal angles.
illustration.caption: Congruent shapes are identical in size and shape; similar shapes have the same shape but may differ in size.

notes.body:
📌 Definition\nTwo shapes are congruent when they have exactly the same size and exactly the same shape.

🔑 Key Concept\nFor two shapes to be congruent:
• All corresponding sides must be equal in length.
• All corresponding angles must be equal in size.
\nThe symbol for congruence is $\cong$. For example, $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$ means triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $DEF$.

💡 Worked Example\nThese two rectangles are congruent:
$$\text{Rectangle A: } 4 \text{ cm by } 6 \text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Rectangle B: } 4 \text{ cm by } 6 \text{ cm}$$\nBoth have the same length, the same width, and the same angles ($90^\circ$ each).

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Congruent shapes fit exactly on top of one another.
• Congruent shapes have equal perimeters and equal areas.
• Reflections, rotations, and translations produce congruent images.

⚠️ Common Mistake\nThinking that shapes with the same angles are automatically congruent. Two rectangles can have four $90^\circ$ angles but different side lengths, so they are not congruent.

notes.heading: Similar Shapes
notes.body:
📌 Definition\nTwo shapes are similar when they have the same shape but not necessarily the same size.

🔑 Key Concept\nFor two shapes to be similar:
• All corresponding angles must be equal.
• All corresponding sides must be in the same ratio.
\nThe symbol for similarity is $\sim$. For example, $\triangle PQR \sim \triangle STU$ means triangle $PQR$ is similar to triangle $STU$.

💡 Worked Example\nTwo rectangles are similar if their sides are in the same ratio:
$$\text{Rectangle A: } 2 \text{ cm by } 4 \text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Rectangle B: } 5 \text{ cm by } 10 \text{ cm}$$\nThe ratio of widths is $2 : 5$ and the ratio of lengths is $4 : 10 = 2 : 5$. Both ratios match, so the rectangles are similar.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Similar shapes have equal corresponding angles.
• The ratio of any pair of corresponding sides is called the scale factor.
• Similar shapes are enlargements or reductions of each other.

⚠️ Common Mistake\nAssuming that shapes with the same area are similar. Two rectangles can both have area $24$ cm$^2$ but very different shapes.

notes.heading: Conditions for Triangle Congruence
notes.body:
📌 Definition\nTo prove that two triangles are congruent, it is enough to show that one of four sets of matching parts is equal.

🔑 Key Concept\nThe four standard tests for triangle congruence are:
• SSS (Side-Side-Side): all three pairs of corresponding sides are equal.
• SAS (Side-Angle-Side): two pairs of sides and the included angle are equal.
• ASA (Angle-Side-Angle): two pairs of angles and the included side are equal.
• RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side): the hypotenuse and one other side of a right-angled triangle are equal.

💡 Worked Example\nConsider two triangles where:
$$AB = DE = 5 \text{ cm}, \quad BC = EF = 7 \text{ cm}, \quad AC = DF = 8 \text{ cm}$$\nBecause all three pairs of sides match, the triangles are congruent by SSS.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The equal angle in SAS must be the included angle between the two sides.
• AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle) alone proves similarity, not congruence.
• RHS only applies to right-angled triangles.

⚠️ Common Mistake\nUsing SSA (Side-Side-Angle) as a congruence test. SSA is not a valid test because it can produce two different triangles.

notes.heading: Scale Factor for Lengths
notes.body:
📌 Definition\nThe scale factor is the ratio of a length on an image to the corresponding length on the original shape.

🔑 How it works\nIf shape $B$ is an enlargement of shape $A$, then:
$$\text{scale factor} = \dfrac{\text{length on } B}{\text{corresponding length on } A}$$
\nTo find a missing length on the image, multiply the original length by the scale factor:
$$\text{image length} = \text{original length} \times \text{scale factor}$$

💡 Worked Example\nA photograph is enlarged so that a side of length $6$ cm becomes $15$ cm. Find the scale factor.
\nStep 1: Divide the new length by the original length.
$$\text{scale factor} = \dfrac{15}{6} = 2.5$$
\nStep 2: Any other original length can now be multiplied by $2.5$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• A scale factor greater than $1$ produces an enlargement.
• A scale factor between $0$ and $1$ produces a reduction.
• The scale factor applies to lengths, not directly to areas.

✅ Check\nIf the scale factor is $2.5$, every length on the image should be $2.5$ times the matching length on the original.

notes.heading: Scale Factor for Areas
notes.body:
📌 Definition\nWhen a shape is enlarged by a linear scale factor $k$, its area is multiplied by $k^2$.

🔑 Key Concept\nIf the length scale factor is $k$, then:
$$\text{area scale factor} = k^2$$
\nThis means:
$$\text{image area} = \text{original area} \times k^2$$

💡 Worked Example\nA rectangle has length $4$ cm and width $3$ cm. It is enlarged by scale factor $3$. Find the area of the enlarged rectangle.
\nStep 1: Find the original area.
$$\text{original area} = 4 \times 3 = 12 \text{ cm}^2$$
\nStep 2: Multiply by the area scale factor.
$$\text{image area} = 12 \times 3^2 = 12 \times 9 = 108 \text{ cm}^2$$

✅ Check\nThe enlarged lengths are $12$ cm and $9$ cm. The area is $12 \times 9 = 108$ cm$^2$, which matches.

⚠️ Common Mistake\nMultiplying the area by the linear scale factor instead of by the square of the scale factor.

notes.heading: Using Ratios in Similar Shapes
notes.body:
📌 Definition\nIn similar shapes, every pair of corresponding lengths is in the same ratio. This ratio can be used to find missing lengths.

🔑 How it works\nSet up a proportion using two pairs of corresponding sides:
$$\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}$$\nwhere $a_1$ and $b_1$ are lengths on the first shape, and $a_2$ and $b_2$ are the corresponding lengths on the second shape.

💡 Worked Example\nTwo similar triangles have corresponding sides $3$ cm and $6$ cm. A second pair of corresponding sides are $5$ cm and $x$ cm. Find $x$.
\nStep 1: Write the ratio of corresponding sides.
$$\dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{5}{x}$$
\nStep 2: Solve for $x$.
$$3x = 30 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x = 10$$
\nThe missing length is $10$ cm.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Always match corresponding sides carefully.
• The scale factor is the same for every pair of corresponding lengths.
• Corresponding angles are equal, so use angles to identify matching sides.

⚠️ Common Mistake\nMatching sides that do not correspond. The longest side on one shape corresponds to the longest side on the other.

notes.heading: Scale Drawings and Maps
notes.body:
📌 Definition\nA scale drawing or map is similar to the real object or area it represents. The scale tells you the ratio between a length on the drawing and the real length.

🔑 Key Concept\nA scale such as $1 : 100$ means $1$ unit on the drawing represents $100$ units in real life. Lengths are multiplied by $100$, but areas are multiplied by $100^2 = 10\,000$.

💡 Worked Example\nA room is drawn as a rectangle $5$ cm by $8$ cm using a scale of $1 : 50$. Find the real area in square metres.
\nStep 1: Find real lengths.
$$5 \times 50 = 250 \text{ cm} = 2.5 \text{ m}$$
$$8 \times 50 = 400 \text{ cm} = 4 \text{ m}$$
\nStep 2: Find the real area.
$$2.5 \times 4 = 10 \text{ m}^2$$
\nThe real area is $10$ m$^2$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Convert drawing lengths to real lengths before finding real area.
• Real area = drawing area $\times$ (scale factor)$^2$ only if both are in the same units.
• Check that units are consistent at each step.

✅ Check\nA quick estimate: $5$ cm by $8$ cm on a $1 : 50$ scale represents about $2.5$ m by $4$ m, giving roughly $10$ m$^2$.

flashcards.definition: Having exactly the same size and exactly the same shape.
flashcards.example: Two triangles with sides $3$ cm, $4$ cm, $5$ cm are congruent to each other.

flashcards.definition: Having the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
flashcards.example: Two rectangles with sides $2$ by $4$ and $5$ by $10$ are similar.

flashcards.definition: The ratio of a length on an image to the corresponding length on the original shape.
flashcards.example: If a $6$ cm side becomes $12$ cm, the scale factor is $2$.

flashcards.definition: Two triangles are congruent if all three pairs of corresponding sides are equal.
flashcards.example: $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$, and $AC = DF$ proves $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$.

flashcards.definition: Two triangles are congruent if two pairs of corresponding sides and the included angle are equal.
flashcards.example: $AB = DE$, $\angle B = \angle E$, and $BC = EF$ proves congruence.

flashcards.definition: Two triangles are congruent if two pairs of corresponding angles and the included side are equal.
flashcards.example: $\angle A = \angle D$, $AB = DE$, and $\angle B = \angle E$ proves congruence.

flashcards.definition: Two right-angled triangles are congruent if their hypotenuses and one other pair of sides are equal.
flashcards.example: In right triangles, equal hypotenuse and one equal leg prove congruence.

flashcards.definition: Sides that occupy the same relative position in two similar or congruent shapes.
flashcards.example: The longest side of one triangle corresponds to the longest side of a similar triangle.

flashcards.definition: Angles that occupy the same relative position in two similar or congruent shapes.
flashcards.example: Matching angles in similar triangles are equal.

flashcards.definition: The factor by which an area changes when a shape is enlarged or reduced.
flashcards.example: For a linear scale factor of $3$, the area scale factor is $3^2 = 9$.

flashcards.definition: The factor by which all lengths change when a shape is enlarged or reduced.
flashcards.example: A scale factor of $0.5$ halves every length.

flashcards.definition: A transformation that produces a similar image larger than the original.
flashcards.example: A scale factor greater than $1$ produces an enlargement.

questions.stem: Which statement is true for two congruent shapes?
choices: They have the same shape but different sizes.
They have the same size and the same shape.
They have equal areas but different perimeters.
questions.explanation: Congruent shapes are identical in both size and shape. They also have equal perimeters and equal areas, and all corresponding angles are equal.

questions.stem: Two triangles are similar. The first has sides $3$ cm, $4$ cm, and $5$ cm. The second has a corresponding side of $9$ cm. What is the scale factor?
questions.explanation: The scale factor is the ratio of corresponding lengths: $9 \div 3 = 3$.

questions.stem: A shape is enlarged by scale factor $4$. By what factor does its area increase?
questions.explanation: Area scales by the square of the linear scale factor. For scale factor $4$, the area factor is $4^2 = 16$.

questions.stem: Which of these is a valid test for triangle congruence?
questions.explanation: SAS (Side-Angle-Side) is a valid congruence test. AAA proves similarity, SSA is not valid, and RHS only applies to right-angled triangles.

questions.stem: Two rectangles are similar. The smaller rectangle is $2$ cm by $6$ cm. The larger rectangle has width $5$ cm. What is its length?
questions.explanation: The ratio of widths is $2 : 5$, so the scale factor is $2.5$. The length is $6 \times 2.5 = 15$ cm.

questions.stem: A triangle has area $20$ cm$^2$. A similar triangle is drawn with scale factor $3$. What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.explanation: The area scale factor is $3^2 = 9$. Therefore the larger area is $20 \times 9 = 180$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides $6$ cm and $9$ cm. A side of length $8$ cm on the first triangle corresponds to a side of length $x$ cm on the second. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: The scale factor is $9 \div 6 = 1.5$. So $x = 8 \times 1.5 = 12$ cm.

questions.stem: Which condition proves that two right-angled triangles are congruent?
choices: Hypotenuse and one other side equal
Two sides equal but not the hypotenuse
questions.explanation: RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) states that two right-angled triangles are congruent if their hypotenuses and one other pair of sides are equal.

questions.stem: A model car is made using scale $1 : 25$. If the real car is $4$ m long, how long is the model in centimetres?
questions.explanation: $4$ m = $400$ cm. With scale $1 : 25$, the model length is $400 \div 25 = 16$ cm.

questions.stem: Two shapes are similar with scale factor $\dfrac{1}{2}$. What happens to the area?
questions.explanation: The area scale factor is the square of the linear scale factor: $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$. So the area is divided by $4$.

questions.stem: A map uses scale $1 : 10\,000$. A field is $4$ cm by $5$ cm on the map. What is the real area in square metres?
Two similar triangles have areas $27$ cm$^2$ and $243$ cm$^2$. What is the linear scale factor from the smaller to the larger?
questions.explanation: The area scale factor is $243 \div 27 = 9$. Since area scale factor = (linear scale factor)$^2$, the linear scale factor is $\sqrt{9} = 3$.

questions.stem: In two congruent triangles, $AB = 7$ cm. What is the length of the corresponding side on the other triangle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides of congruent triangles are equal in length, so the matching side is also $7$ cm.

questions.stem: A rectangle with length $8$ cm and width $5$ cm is enlarged by scale factor $2$. What is the perimeter of the enlarged rectangle?
questions.explanation: The enlarged length is $8 \times 2 = 16$ cm and the enlarged width is $5 \times 2 = 10$ cm. The perimeter is $2(16 + 10) = 52$ cm.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of triangles must be similar?
choices: Two triangles with the same perimeter
questions.explanation: All equilateral triangles have angles of $60^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $60^\circ$, so their corresponding angles are equal and they are always similar. The other options do not guarantee similarity.
